## GET /admin-api/backup-codes

`getBackupCodesSettings`

**The recovery-code mechanism's settings, and what a code is**

The four `backupCodes.*` settings — whether a set is issued at all, how many codes are in one, how long each is, and how it is broken up for reading — with the mechanism itself in `status`, read from `common/backup_codes.ts` rather than written down here.

**THIS IS THE ONLY MECHANISM IN THIS SERVICE THAT NO SPECIFICATION DEFINES.** There is no RFC for a recovery code, so `status` has no specification column: every field in it is a decision this service made, and `bitsPerCode` is the one worth reading first.

**A PERSON GENERATES THEIR OWN SET** on /portal/mfa, is shown it once, and it is stored as one scrypt hash per code only when they confirm they have kept it; generating again replaces it. Nothing on this API issues a set and nothing on it reads a code back; `POST /users/clear-backup-codes` deletes one.

**CHANGING THESE AFFECTS NEW SETS ONLY, AND NO EXISTING SET IS INVALIDATED** — unlike `totp.*`, this needs no paragraph about enrolments, because nothing here was told to an app this service cannot reach. A recovery code is compared against its stored hash.

Who holds a set is `GET /users`, which reports the counts and never the codes.

THERE IS NO POST BESIDE THIS ONE and that is not a gap: every form on the console page this mirrors posts `set-many` to /admin/config, so `POST /admin-api/config/set-many` is already the operation for it. One store, one action, two doors.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/backup-codes` on the admin console.

The reply also carries `protocolEndpoints`: every endpoint of this family in the realm the call arrived in, as `{ name, methods, url }` (plus `route` for an HTTP endpoint, `transport` for a socket, and `registered: false` for a route the router no longer has).

Scope: `admin:read`.
